submission_document.task-prompt:
Nadia at Piedmont Ridge wants the Larkspur Crossing liens dealt with before the refinance closes on November 20, and Marguerite has to tell her by the end of the month which claims we demand released and which the bank will make us bond. I'm the paralegal on the Piedmont Ridge account at Ferraro Whitcombe in Sacramento, California, and the first analysis on every lien file the office defends starts with me. I am in trial in Redding through the 16th, so I am handing this one to you because you have worked mechanics lien claims in this office for years and can read a waiver form against a check register without the Code open beside you. The file is in the folder: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx, claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx, owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx, dk_subcontractor_payments.csv, and completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx. The claims are our transcriptions of the recorder's copies with whatever each claimant attached, and the payments file is what Dunmore-Kettle's controller sent when Marguerite asked for it.

Build the analysis as one workbook named lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx. The first tab is what Marguerite reads: for each recorded claim, whether the claimant has lien rights at all, whether the claim was recorded in time, what the waivers on file do to it, the amount the claimant could actually enforce against the property, what we do about it, and what a release bond would have to be for each lien we cannot clear. Behind it I want the dates worked from the notice of completion under the practice note, the preliminary notices and the waivers checked claimant by claimant against the payments, and each enforceable amount built up so that Marguerite can follow every dollar to the claim or the ledger it came from. Put a note to Marguerite on the last tab with anything the file leaves open and anything that cuts against what Nadia expects. Nadia's position with the bank is that every claim is either late, waived, or Dunmore-Kettle's to answer, and if the record says otherwise Marguerite needs to hear it from us first. I need the workbook by Tuesday, October 20.

repeatable-bfbf1.textarea-rubric_description: The deliverable is a single workbook named exactly lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx whose first worksheet states the standing of each of the 7 recorded claims.

The first worksheet's release bonds required total reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the claim-by-claim standing behind it, or a sum over the same per-claim bonds alike, standing at $399,425.55.
The last day for a claimant other than the direct contractor to record is stated as 09/21/2026 because the thirtieth day after the notice of completion fell on a Saturday.
Ostrowski Electric's claim recorded 09/21/2026 is found timely.
Calder Drywall's claim recorded 09/22/2026 is found untimely.
Norcal Rebar is found to have no lien rights because its preliminary notice was given to the direct contractor and never to the owner.
Tallac Concrete's lien is found expired because no action was commenced within 90 days after its recording.
Hedrick & Sons' enforceable amount is stated as $33,982.19 on the first worksheet.
Kastner Mechanical's enforceable amount is stated as $159,145 on the first worksheet.
Bautista Painting's enforceable amount is stated as $8,125 on the first worksheet.
The first worksheet carries all 7 recorded claims, 3 of them routed to a demand for release.
The amount the claimants could enforce against the property is stated as $262,729.19 on the first worksheet.
The recorded amount of the claims to demand released is stated as $99,830.00.
The three claims that cannot be enforced are routed to a demand for release under section 8482 as the first step.
The note to Marguerite is the last worksheet.
The note tells Marguerite that the direct contractor can still record a claim until 10/19/2026.
The workbook wrongly treats the HVAC subcontractor's conditional waiver through 07/31/2026 as releasing the July payment although check 4460 was stopped.
The workbook wrongly treats the painting subcontractor's unconditional waiver through 07/31/2026 as ineffective for want of payment although section 8134 makes it effective when signed.
The workbook wrongly measures a release bond by the enforceable amount although section 8424(b) sets it at 125 percent of the claim as recorded.
The workbook wrongly includes the lumber supplier's April deliveries in its enforceable amount although its late preliminary notice reaches back only twenty days before it was given.
The workbook wrongly starts the 30 days at the completion date rather than at the recording of the notice of completion.
The workbook wrongly treats the site concrete subcontractor's lien release letter as releasing the May balance although it is not in the statutory form.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as a lien analysis the partner can act on with the bank's counsel.

The bank requires all recorded lien claims to be released of record or bonded by November 6. Marguerite needs to tell Nadia by end of month which claims to demand released and which must be bonded. The analysis must determine for each of seven recorded claims: lien rights, timeliness, waiver effects, enforceable amount, recommended action, and bond amount where needed.

The instructions name five input files: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx, claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx, owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx, dk_subcontractor_payments.csv, and completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx. Each file's actual contents match its described purpose.

Behind it, supporting tabs with dates worked from the notice of completion under the practice note, preliminary notices and waivers checked claimant-by-claimant against payments, and enforceable amounts built up with traceable figures. Material constraints are stated: (1) Delivery deadline: Tuesday, October 20. (2) Refinance closing: November 20, 2026. (3) Bank's lien clearance deadline: November 6. (4) The practice note (PN-14) provides the analytical framework, counting conventions, and legal standards to apply—including specific Civil Code sections, date-counting rules, waiver validation procedures, and bond calculation (125% of recorded amount). (5) Nadia's position (every claim is late, waived, or DK's to answer) must be tested and contradicted where the record says otherwise. (6) The analysis must follow the office's established methodology per the practice note. No missing material constraints were identified; the scenario is self-contained with all necessary dates, legal standards, and analytical requirements.

coverage.reason: For each of the 7 claimants, preliminary notice data is available from the owner's Prelim Log (13 entries covering all direct-contractor subs) and the claims themselves (which attach proof of service where applicable). The practice note specifies how to evaluate lien rights (§1). Norcal Rebar's notice to the owner is deliberately ambiguous—Exhibit A shows service only on the contractor, the Prelim Log has no Norcal entry, and Reid's correspondence confirms uncertainty—but the practice note §5 instructs the analyst to flag such gaps. All data needed to assess lien rights is present or the gap is an intended analytical finding.

The notice of completion was recorded August 20, 2026 (completion date August 11, 2026, within the 15-day window). All seven claims have recording dates in the claims file. The practice note §2 provides counting rules (CCP §12/12a). For subcontractors, the deadline is 30 days after NOC recording; for the direct contractor, 60 days. Calendar computation (weekends/holidays) is ordinary professional knowledge. All necessary dates are supplied.

The Waiver Log in owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx lists every waiver received, with form title, through-date, amount, exceptions, check reference, and dates. The DK subcontractor payment CSV provides check status (cleared/stopped) to validate conditional waivers. The practice note §3 specifies how to read each waiver form type. Key scenarios are all tractable: Kastner's conditional waiver on stopped check 4460, Bautista's unconditional waiver through 07/31 despite no payment, Tallac's non-statutory lien release letter, Ostrowski's conditional waiver on cleared check 4461, Calder's unconditional waivers through 06/30. No waiver for Norcal Rebar or Hedrick appears, which is consistent with them being sub-tier suppliers not paid by DK.

For direct-contractor subcontractors (Tallac, Kastner, Bautista, Ostrowski, Calder), the subcontract values are in the Subcontractors sheet, payments are in the CSV, waivers define what's released, and claim amounts are in the claims file. For sub-tier suppliers (Norcal Rebar, Hedrick), the claims include their own account statements or claim amounts. Hedrick's Exhibit A provides invoice-level detail with payments noted. For Norcal, the Tallac-to-Norcal payment history is not in the file, but the practice note §5 instructs the analyst to flag missing documents rather than guess—this is an expected analytical output, not a missing input. The practice note §3.1 and §1.2 (late preliminary notice window) provide the rules for computing enforceable amounts.

Practice note §4 specifies the owner's remedies: demand release for untimely/unenforceable liens, or bond at 125% of recorded amount for enforceable ones. The civil index search (no pending actions) and recorder search (no releases, no notice of credit) are provided in completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx §D. The bank's November 6 recording deadline and November 20 closing date are stated in Nadia's correspondence. All recorded claim amounts are stated in the claims file, so bond computations (125% × recorded amount) can be performed.

The instructions require flagging anything the file leaves open and anything that cuts against Nadia's position. The supplied evidence contains several such items: (a) Norcal's preliminary notice to the owner is unconfirmed, (b) Tallac's lien release letter is non-statutory and may not release the lien, (c) Kastner's check was stopped so the conditional waiver is ineffective, (d) Bautista signed an unconditional waiver but was never paid, (e) Hedrick's preliminary notice was late so the enforceable amount is reduced, (f) the Kastner airflow deficiency and $22,000 correction cost, (g) DK's threat to record its own claim. All of these are identifiable from the supplied files. The practice note §5 instructs the analyst to name documents that would resolve open points.

The instructions specify a workbook named lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx with a summary tab, supporting date/notice/waiver tabs, and a note-to-Marguerite tab. fields.description:
Press this at any point while you work on this section. It reviews:

  • Rubric rows — every criterion has a description and a weight between -5 and +5
  • Scoring — at least one weight is positive, so a correct deliverable can score
  • Depth — advisory note on whether the rubric covers the task's complexity

This feedback is advisory and does not submit or block anything.

sections.description:
List your criteria one by one — most tasks will need a minimum of 3 criteria; expect somewhere in the 20–60+ range depending on complexity. Each line should test exactly one thing: a specific number, name, date, format requirement, or structural detail — not a bundled description.

  • Weight -5 to +5 based on how central the item is to a correct deliverable.
  • Use negative weights where useful, to penalize specific unwanted outcomes (extra items included that shouldn't be, page limit exceeded, wrong file type).
  • Pull every exact value straight from your own reference files and ground-truth answer — never estimate what a criterion should check.
    • Bad (estimated): [+2] The workbook states total damage revenue as approximately $15,000.
    • Good (pulled from the actual data): [+2] The workbook states total damage revenue as $15,170.
  • End with a general "Overall formatting and style of the deliverable" line (commonly ~+5) to catch polish and presentation.

sections.title: Before You Submit — Task Creation Checklist

fields.label: Confirm each item below applies to your submission before you check it off. All boxes must be checked to submit.

options.label: Task Instruction: My instruction sets specific context: a named role, organization, and a reason this work is happening today.
Task Instruction: I named every input file I'm uploading and briefly described what each one contains.
Task Instruction: I stated the exact deliverable format (file type), plus any length or structural requirements (page limit, tab count, required columns, naming convention).
Task Instruction: I included real scenario constraints where they belong (budget, deadline, headcount, threshold).
Task Instruction: I did not include any number, name, or finding that can only come from actually working through the input files — those live in the rubric, not here.
Task Instruction: My instruction is fully self-contained: someone with no rubric access could read it and my input files and have everything they need to produce a complete, correct answer.
Input Files: Every file I listed is actually uploaded, and every file I uploaded is listed — names match exactly, including extension and case.
Input Files: I'm only using files I'm authorized to share — no confidential, proprietary, or IP-restricted material.
Task Rubric: I have at least 3 criteria, and enough to genuinely cover the task's complexity (most real tasks need well more than 3).
Task Rubric: Each criterion tests exactly one thing — no line bundles two separate checks with "and."
Task Rubric: Each criterion's weight (-5 to +5) reflects how central that item actually is to a correct deliverable.
Task Rubric: My rubric ends with a general "Overall formatting and style of the deliverable" line.
Task Rubric: Nothing in my rubric asserts a fact that isn't actually derivable from the input files I'm providing.
Final Check: If someone with real expertise in this domain — but no access to my rubric — read only my instruction and files, they could produce work that passes my rubric.
